links.note: Greek resumes the subject with “that one” before “is.”
English supplies the understood object of “opens.”
Greek says “all his own” with “sheep” understood.
English compresses “what were the things which” into “what.”
Greek says the sheep “are not his own.”
English names the sheep where Greek uses “them.”
Greek says “my own know me” while English uses passive voice.
The participle means a person possessed by a demon.
English adds a confirming question tag.
Greek asks literally how long they will “lift our soul,” meaning keep them in suspense.
Greek combines double negation with “for the age” to express “never.”
English uses a possessive where Greek has “the Father.”
